question: 2024 has just begun and is a European election year. We are at a crossroads in Europe and the world; it is in an election year and voting is always important. It is one of the most noble ways for people to exercise their citizenship, especially at a time when we are facing populisms and extremisms as they attack and undermine European democracies.
I would therefore like to ask how the Commission will encourage Europeans to vote. The tasks we have ahead of us are fundamental, but voting and thus defending democracy is no less important.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.3.2024) The Commission attaches great importance to supporting high voter turnout and continues to actively support Member States’ efforts in this regard.

In December 2023, the Commission issued a recommendation1 on free, fair, inclusive and resilient elections to Member States and political actors, as part of the ‘Defence of Democracy Package’ which builds democratic resilience from within. The recommendation encourages the inclusion of citizen observers in electoral processes.

Member States can integrate citizen observers’ input in the national reports submitted to the European Parliament. The Commission closely cooperates with the European Parliament to create a one-stop-shop for the interinstitutional campaign promoting turnout in the European elections in 2024.

The website dedicated to these elections also includes detailed ‘How to vote’ pages, which were updated with the help of the Member States in the framework of the European Cooperation Network on Elections (ECNE)2. A particular focus is put on promoting the participation of all groups and addressing their specific needs.

This is done by directly addressing citizens, for example through EU-wide getout-to-vote campaigns, by providing common EU channels for informing citizens where and how to register and vote, through EU funding of civil society, and promoting the recently released ‘Guide to EU citizenship’3.

A Compendium of e-voting and other ICT4 practices and a ‘Guide of good electoral practices in Member States addressing participation of citizens with disabilities in the electoral process’5 prepared in close cooperation with ECNE have been published as part of a ‘Citizenship Package’ adopted in December 2023, in time for the European elections in 2024.
